americano.title: Americano
americano.howItWorks: Partners rotate every round, everyone plays everyone, most points wins. With the field in fours the schedule is exact: every pair partners once, and the rotation completes after players-minus-one rounds (7 rounds for 8 players); the next round starts over from round 1. Reserved players who haven't accepted yet count for round 1.

about.title: The fine print, kept short
about.sub: No lawyers were harmed. Here's what Kicksmash does with your stuff.
about.storeBody: Your name, the matches you organize or join, scores, and, only if you give them, your email and phone. That's it. Your identity lives in a cookie on your device plus a private link, no password.
about.neverBody: Sell your data. Show ads. Email you for fun. Emails only go out for things you asked for: calendar invites, updates to matches you're in, reminders you switched on, and invitations an organizer sent you (with a one-tap 'never again' link).
about.cookiesBody: One functional cookie that remembers who you are, one for your language. No tracking, no third-party cookies, no banner needed.
about.rightsBody: Change your name or email anytime. Turn notifications off. Delete your account from My matches: your personal data disappears, your old scores stay as 'Deleted player' so your friends' history still adds up. Want a copy of your data? Email us.
about.termsBody: It's free. Be nice, show up, enter the score. The app comes as-is with no warranty; if a link breaks or a court double-books, that's between you and your padel buddies. We can remove abusive content or accounts.
about.openBody: Kicksmash is open source under the Apache 2.0 license. Read it, run it, build on it. The name and logo stay ours.

levels.title: What your padel level means
levels.sub: Kicksmash uses the 0 to 7 scale most padel apps use, in quarter steps. You declare it once; results move it a little; an organizer who played with you can confirm it.
levels.scaleNote: The same numbers Playtomic-style apps show, so a 3.0 here means what a 3.0 means at your club.
levels.rangesHelp: An organizer can set a range. Inside it people join; outside it they ask, and the organizer decides. Presets:
levels.faq1q: How do I know my level?
levels.faq1a: Read the scale above and pick the band that describes most of your matches, not your best day. Most people who play weekly and use the glass on purpose are 2.5 to 3.5. If unsure, pick the lower number: results correct it upwards.
levels.faq2q: How does the level change after matches?
levels.faq2a: Only when an organizer confirms a 2v2 score or finalizes a tournament. The change is small (at most ±{match} per match, ±{tournament} per tournament) and depends on the levels of everyone involved: beating stronger players moves you more. Unrated players never move anyone.
levels.faq3q: What is the tick next to a level?
levels.faq3a: An organizer who played with that person confirmed the level after the result. It stays while the level moves less than half a step. Rankings can rely on it.
levels.faq4a: It shows as a small chip next to your first name on matches you are in. Club and city rankings list you only if you switch that on yourself.
levels.ctaHelp: No account. Your name and level live behind a personal link.
levels.metaDescription: The padel level scale explained: what 0 to 7 means, how results move it, what a confirmed level is, and how level ranges work on a match.
